g.text: Larder against llama.cpp: the same model on the same computer

text.style: font-size: 9.6px; font-family: 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #52514e

g.text: How many times faster, each grid line doubles. The faded part of a bar: the spread over prompt lengths, runs or orders.
llama.cpp b11719 at the fastest setting of a sweep; quality not compared in this chart. Mac, 16 GB M4, 2026-11-06, one run per cell, not like for
like: Larder ran a mixed 4/2-bit research pack (about 3 bits) with the model's MTP head, from the internal SSD plus about 11 GB a
request from an external USB4 SSD; llama.cpp ran a 4.25-bit IQ4_XS from that external SSD alone; 1k, 4k and 16k prompts.
PC, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB, 15 GB RAM. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, 2026-11-06: Larder's 4-bit research pack (60.9 GB of experts) against unsloth's UD-Q4_K_XL
(77 GB), exact routing on both sides; stock llama.cpp swapped past the memory guard while loading, so its row is llama.cpp with
Larder's expert store patched in; short and 8k prompts, the first token at 8k one run. 35B, 2026-11-11, one session, both orders: llama.cpp's Q4_0 GGUF at
--n-cpu-moe 11 (its best that fits) against Larder on the same experts. The recipe is what ./larder installs: cache bias 0.5, which passed its paired
quality gate, and the model's MTP head. Exact routing: cache bias 0, no head. Short decode: turns 2-3; an 8k prompt: 8,074 / 8,086 tokens.
